programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: After losing his Xavier Academy job last season over the unfortunate Coach Keenan saga, Gerry finds himself subbing at a tough inner city school, miserable and desperate to get his old job back. Meanwhile, the Xavier staff is concerned about Robert, whose attempt to cultivate a cool new laid back image is misconstrued for a nervous breakdown due to his having been overlooked as Principal Callaghan’s successor. At the same time, Trudy’s patience is tested when Emma’s husband Ted decides to hang out for the day while his wife works.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: Gerry is assigned an educational assistant, Marty, who quickly becomes a new source of irritation in the classroom as he continually challenges Gerry’s authority while helping students cheat on tests. His first pupil, Simon, discovers the hard way that Dwyer might not be in the right headspace to teach beginner level guitar. Meanwhile, Bobbi is stuck sharing her lunch hours with the most annoying student at Xavier.

programme.title: Mr. D
programme.desc: When Lisa asks Gerry to cover coaching duties for the upcoming wrestling tournament, Gerry promises to bring home two trophies. At the same time, Simon has a spiritual awakening after discovering his Jewish roots; while Lisa is confused when Frank breaks up with her.

programme.desc: Officers uncover deeper layers of criminal activity within seemingly routine cases, exposing new illegal acts in the process, from corrupt officials to hidden criminal networks.

programme.title: Newsfront
programme.desc: The normalization of antisemitism in America by politicians and public figures leads to unprecedented attacks against the Jewish community.

programme.title: The World Seen From the Vatican

programme.sub-title: The World Seen From the Vatican

programme.title: Wake Up America Weekend
programme.desc: Wake up smarter with Kyle Lowder and Kenzie Beach as they deliver the latest headlines, insightful analysis, and lively discussion to keep you ahead of the day’s biggest stories.

programme.desc: Tom Basile tackles the week’s biggest stories with top talkers from politics, Hollywood, and across America.

programme.title: Saturday Report
programme.desc: Rita Cosby tackles the big headlines with smart analysis from top experts.

programme.title: Saturday Agenda
programme.desc: Rob Astorino reveals Washington’s inner workings and the fight for core values.

programme.title: Rob Carson’s What in the World?

programme.sub-title: Rob Carson’s What in the World?

programme.title: Newsmax News In-Depth
programme.desc: Bianca de la Garza looks at the big stories of the week, politics, policy, the economy, and much more!

programme.desc: Greg Kelly gives hardest-hitting reports and analysis from L.A. to N.Y., from Beltway to Rust Belt, talking with you and for you!

programme.title: Jon Chandonnet
programme.desc: News - Jon Chandonnet was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 1996, and as an active grad student at MIT, he responded by pushing his body to the limits. He ran marathons and climbed mountains to prove MS was not slowing him down. Six years later, that pace caught up with him. In this episode, Mathew Embry talks with Jon about denying the diagnosis, what changed when symptoms hit hard, and how MS demands a different kind of discipline. Jon shares how targeting inflammation through diet and lifestyle became a turning point, and how redefining strength has helped him keep moving forward.

programme.title: Jon Chandonnet
programme.desc: News - Jon Chandonnet was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 1996, and as an active grad student at MIT, he responded by pushing his body to the limits. He ran marathons and climbed mountains to prove MS was not slowing him down. Six years later, that pace caught up with him. In this episode, Mathew Embry talks with Jon about denying the diagnosis, what changed when symptoms hit hard, and how MS demands a different kind of discipline. Jon shares how targeting inflammation through diet and lifestyle became a turning point, and how redefining strength has helped him keep moving forward.

programme.title: Oceans of Hope
programme.desc: News - Oceans of Hope began with a simple but radical question: what if people living with multiple sclerosis were invited onto a sailing vessel as crew, not observers? In this episode, Mathew Embry speaks with Dr. Mikkel Anthonisen, a medical doctor, lifelong sailor, and the founder of Oceans of Hope, a global sailing expedition for those affected by MS. He is joined by filmmaker and sailor Ellia Rhodes, who documents one of the voyages and its impact. Together, they explore how sailing as active participants builds confidence, trust, and possibility in the face of chronic illness.
